scope: Mathematical review only, before viewing any new residual finite-difference values. No source, build, or model actions.

finding.statement: One-sided slope-gap <=1% is not a valid acceptance gate for a squared residual cost at finite eta. The residual objective is quadratic even when the underlying observation h is exactly affine, so its one-sided slopes differ by an expected O(eta) curvature term while its central FD equals the exact derivative.
finding.required_action: For full, midpoint, and terminal squared-residual cost components, gate on central FD-versus-AD <=1% at both widths, adjacent central-FD plateau <=1%, and resolved central signal. Report one-sided cost slopes/gaps as diagnostics only. Keep the already-frozen <=1% one-sided tests on the underlying linear h_mid/h_terminal diagnostics as the separate map-branch/directional consistency check; do not introduce a new threshold or claim classical smoothness.

synthetic_exact_affine_counterexample.conclusion: Both central checks are exact while both cost one-sided gaps exceed 1%; applying the old linear-objective one-sided gate to cost would falsely reject this smooth, exactly differentiated quadratic.

signal_floor.note: Use a local baseline magnitude bound per component and their sum for the full objective. Keep this only for signal resolution; use no floor in FD/AD relative-error or width-plateau denominators.

midpoint_component_guard: The terminal residual FD guard and the midpoint residual FD check remain separate; the scaled old-terminal gradient guard must use central FD, plateau and signal gates, while its underlying linear h_N one-sided check remains the pre-existing branch diagnostic.
data_boundary: No new residual FD values were inspected or used to choose this correction. Freeze this rule before revealing them.
